PM Cluster 2

```{r}

f.PCAdata.PM.2 <- filter(f.PCAdata.PM, cluster == "Cluster 2") # Extract the data just for Females in PM Cluster 2
row.names(f.PCAdata.PM.2) <- f.PCAdata.PM.2$TOPPID

#First exploratory PCA with all data, including Isotopes
PCA.f.1.PM.2 <- prcomp(f.PCAdata.PM.2[c(5:25)], center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
summary(PCA.f.1.PM.2)
get_eigenvalue(PCA.f.1.PM.2)

# Plot the PCs to look at variance explained
pdf("../figures/PCAVariance_PM2.pdf")
screeplot(PCA.f.1.PM.2, type = "l", npcs = 10, main = "Screeplot of the first 10 PCs")
abline(h = 1, col="red", lty=5)
legend("topright", legend=c("Eigenvalue = 1"),
       col=c("red"), lty=5, cex=0.6)
dev.off()

screeplot(PCA.f.1.PM.2, type = "l", npcs = 10, main = "Screeplot of the first 10 PCs")
abline(h = 1, col="red", lty=5)
legend("topright", legend=c("Eigenvalue = 1"),
       col=c("red"), lty=5, cex=0.6)

# Cumulative proportion
cumpro <- cumsum(PCA.f.1.PM.2$sdev^2 / sum(PCA.f.1.PM.2$sdev^2))
pdf("../figures/PCACumulativeVariance_PM2.pdf")
plot(cumpro[0:10], xlab = "PC #", ylab = "Amount of explained variance", main = "Cumulative variance plot")
abline(v = 6, col="blue", lty=5)
abline(h = 0.84787     , col="blue", lty=5) # Cumulative variance explained by the 10 PCs
legend("topleft", legend=c("Cut-off @ PC 6"),
       col=c("blue"), lty=5, cex=0.6)
dev.off()

plot(cumpro[0:10], xlab = "PC #", ylab = "Amount of explained variance", main = "Cumulative variance plot")
abline(v = 6, col="blue", lty=5)
abline(h = 0.84787     , col="blue", lty=5) # Cumulative variance explained by the 10 PCs
legend("topleft", legend=c("Cut-off @ PC 6"),
       col=c("blue"), lty=5, cex=0.6)

# Check the loadings and scores
pdf("../figures/PCAScores_PM2.pdf")
autoplot(PCA.f.1.PM.2, data = f.PCAdata.PM.2, colour = 'ProcedureYear', loadings = TRUE, 
         loadings.colour = 'blue',loadings.label = TRUE, loadings.label.size = 3, main = "Year")
dev.off()

# Fancy plot with ellipses
f <- fviz_pca_ind(PCA.f.1.PM.2, geom.ind = "point", pointshape = 21, 
             pointsize = 2, 
             fill.ind = as.factor(f.PCAdata.PM.2$ProcedureYear), 
             col.ind = "black", 
             palette = "simpsons", 
             addEllipses = TRUE,
             label = "var",
             col.var = "black",
             repel = TRUE,
             legend.title = "Year") +
  ggtitle("2D PCA-plot from trip variables") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(f)

ggsave(filename = "../figures/PCAGroups_PM2.pdf",
       plot = f,
       device = cairo_pdf)
# HCPC with 6 PCs
fPCAhc.PM.2 <- scale(f.PCAdata.PM.2[c(5:25)])
res.pca.f.1.PM.2 <- PCA(fPCAhc.PM.2, ncp = 6, graph = FALSE)

# Extract the loadings
loadings.pca.f.1.PM.2 <- sweep(res.pca.f.1.PM.2$var$coord,2,sqrt(res.pca.f.1.PM.2$eig[1:ncol(res.pca.f.1.PM.2$var$coord),1]),FUN="/")
 
# Rotate the loadings 
loadings.pca.f.1.PM.2 <- varimax(loadings.pca.f.1.PM.2)$loadings

# Replace the values using the rotated
res.pca.f.1.PM.2$var$coord <- loadings.pca.f.1.PM.2
pca.var <- get_pca(res.pca.f.1.PM.2, element = c("var", "ind"))

coord <- pca.var[["coord"]]
contrib <- pca.var[["contrib"]]

write.csv(coord,'../results/PCAcoord_PM2.csv')
write.csv(contrib,'../results/PCAcontrib_PM2.csv')


# Compute hierarchical clustering on principal components
res.hcpc.1.PM.2 <- HCPC(res.pca.f.1.PM.2, 
                        kk = Inf, 
                        min = 2, 
                        max  = 10, 
                        metric = "euclidean", 
                        method = "ward", 
                        consol = TRUE,
                        graph = FALSE)

plot(res.hcpc.1.PM.2) # 2 clusters

# Check that k is right
ind.PCAPM.2 <- get_pca_ind(res.pca.f.1.PM.2)
ind.PCAPM.2 <- data.frame(ind.PCAPM.2$coord[,1:6])
#ind.PCAPM <- tibble::rownames_to_column(ind.PCAPM, "AnimalID")
#col2keep <- c("Dim.1","Dim.2","Dim.3","Dim.4","Dim.5", "Dim.6")
#ind.PCAM2 <- ind.PCAPM[,col2keep]

res.nbclust <- NbClust(ind.PCAPM.2, distance = "euclidean",
                       min.nc = 2, max.nc = 15, 
                       method = "ward.D", index ="alllong")

# Agree that 2 is the correct number of clusters
# Compute hierarchical clustering on principal components
res.hcpc.1.PM.2 <- HCPC(res.pca.f.1.PM.2,
                      nb.clust = 2,
                      metric = "euclidean", 
                      method = "ward", 
                      graph = FALSE)

f <- fviz_dend(res.hcpc.1.PM.2, 
          cex = 0.7,                     # Label size
          palette = "jco",               # Color palette see ?ggpubr::ggpar
          rect = TRUE, rect_fill = TRUE, # Add rectangle around groups
          rect_border = "jco",           # Rectangle color
          labels_track_height = 0.8,      # Augment the room for labels
          main = "Cluster analysis  - PM Cluster 2"
                    )

print(f)

ggsave(filename = "../figures/PCA_HCPC_PM2.pdf",
       plot = f,
       device = cairo_pdf)

# Bi-space
fviz_cluster(res.hcpc.1.PM.2,
             repel = TRUE,            # Avoid label overlapping
             show.clust.cent = TRUE, # Show cluster centers
             palette = "jco",         # Color palette see ?ggpubr::ggpar
             ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
             main = "Factor map"
             )
print(f)

ggsave(filename = "../figures/PCA_HCPC2D_PM2.pdf",
       plot = f,
       device = cairo_pdf)

#Add the clusters to the original dataset

f.PCAdata.PM.2$IntCluster <- paste('SubCluster',res.hcpc.1.PM.2$data.clust$clust)
write.csv(f.PCAdata.PM.2,'../results/PM_Cluster2.csv')

################################################################################################################################################################################################################

# Extract the PCA values
ind.PCAPM.2 <- get_pca_ind(PCA.f.1.PM.2)
ind.PCAPM.2 <- data.frame(ind.PCAPM.2$coord[,1:6])
ind.PCAPM.2 <- tibble::rownames_to_column(ind.PCAPM.2, "AnimalID")

d <- 6
Psi <- crossprod(matrix(rnorm(d^2), d, d)) # scale

temp <-  tibble::rownames_to_column(f.PCAdata.PM.2, "AnimalID")
data4Niche.PM.2 <- merge(temp, ind.PCAPM.2, by = 'AnimalID')

#data4Niche.PM <- data4Niche.PM[!data4Niche.PM$cluster == "Cluster 4",] #Get rid of cluster 4

aggregate(data4Niche.PM.2[30:35], data4Niche.PM.2[29], mean)

# Generate parameter draws
nsamples <- 1e4
system.time({
 PM2.par <- tapply(1:nrow(data4Niche.PM.2), data4Niche.PM.2$IntCluster,
                    function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = data4Niche.PM.2[ii,30:35], Psi = Psi))
})


# various parameter plots
clrs <- c("#a6cee3",
          "#1f78b4",
          "#b2df8a",
          "#33a02c") # colors for each cluster

# Plot all mu 
pdf("../figures/PostMu_PM2.pdf")
niche.par.plot(PM2.par, col = clrs, plot.mu = TRUE, plot.Sigma = FALSE)
legend("topleft", legend = names(PM2.par), fill = clrs)
dev.off()

niche.par.plot(PM2.par, col = clrs, plot.mu = TRUE, plot.Sigma = FALSE)
legend("topleft", legend = names(PM2.par), fill = clrs)

# Plot all Sigma 
pdf("../figures/PostSigma_PM2.pdf")
par(mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
niche.par.plot(PM2.par, col = clrs, plot.mu = FALSE, plot.Sigma = TRUE)
legend("topleft", legend = names(PM2.par), fill = clrs)
dev.off()

par(mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
niche.par.plot(PM2.par, col = clrs, plot.mu = FALSE, plot.Sigma = TRUE)
legend("topleft", legend = names(PM2.par), fill = clrs)

# 2-d projections of 50 niche regions
nsamples <- 50
PM2.par <- tapply(1:nrow(data4Niche.PM.2), data4Niche.PM.2$IntCluster,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = data4Niche.PM.2[ii,30:35], Psi = Psi))

# format data for plotting function
PM2.data <- tapply(1:nrow(data4Niche.PM.2), data4Niche.PM.2$IntCluster, function(ii) X = data4Niche.PM.2[ii,30:35])

pdf("../figures/NicheRegionsPM2.pdf")
niche.plot(niche.par = PM2.par, niche.data = PM2.data, pfrac = .05,
          iso.names = c('PCA1','PCA2','PCA3','PCA4','PCA5','PCA6'),
            col = clrs, xlab = expression("PCA Scores"))
dev.off()

niche.plot(niche.par = PM2.par, niche.data = PM2.data, pfrac = .05,
          iso.names = c('PCA1','PCA2','PCA3','PCA4','PCA5','PCA6'),
            col = clrs, xlab = expression("PCA Scores"))

#########################

# niche overlap plots for 95% niche region sizes
nsamples <- 10000
PM2.par <- tapply(1:nrow(data4Niche.PM.2), data4Niche.PM.2$IntCluster,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = data4Niche.PM.2[ii,30:35], Psi = Psi))

# Overlap calculation.  use nsamples = nprob = 10000 (1e4) for higher accuracy.
# the variable over.stat can be supplied directly to the overlap.plot function

over.stat.PM2 <- overlap(PM2.par, nreps = nsamples, nprob = 1e4, alpha = c(.95, 0.99))

#The mean overlap metrics calculated across iterations for both niche 
#region sizes (alpha = .95 and alpha = .99) can be calculated and displayed in an array.
over.mean.PM2 <- apply(over.stat.PM2, c(1:2,4), mean)*100
round(over.mean.PM2, 2)

# Credibility Intervals
over.cred.PM2 <- apply(over.stat.PM2*100, c(1:2, 4), quantile, prob = c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE)
round(over.cred.PM2[,,,1]) # display alpha = .95 niche region

# Overlap plot
over.stat.PM2 <- overlap(PM2.par, nreps = nsamples, nprob = 1e4, alpha = .95)
pdf("../figures/NicheOverlapPM2.pdf")
overlap.plot(over.stat.PM2, col = clrs, mean.cred.col = "turquoise", equal.axis = TRUE,
            xlab = "Overlap Probability (%) -- Niche Region Size: 95%")
dev.off()

overlap.plot(over.stat.PM2, col = clrs, mean.cred.col = "turquoise", equal.axis = TRUE,
            xlab = "Overlap Probability (%) -- Niche Region Size: 95%")

################################################################################
###############################   Niche Size   #################################

# posterior distribution of (mu, Sigma) for each strategy
nsamples <- 10000
PM2.par <- tapply(1:nrow(data4Niche.PM.2), data4Niche.PM.2$IntCluster,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = data4Niche.PM.2[ii,30:35], Psi = Psi))

# posterior distribution of niche size by species using the 75% contour to define strategy niche
PM2.size <- sapply(PM2.par, function(spec) {
  apply(spec$Sigma, 3, niche.size, alpha = .75)
})

# point estimate and standard error
rbind(est = colMeans(PM2.size),
      se = apply(PM2.size, 2, sd))

# Niche Size
PM2.size2 <- matrix(NA, nrow = 20000, ncol = 2)
colnames(PM2.size2) <- c("Niche_Size", "SubCluster")
PM2.size2[1:10000,1] <- PM2.size[,1]
PM2.size2[1:10000,2] <- colnames(PM2.size)[1]
PM2.size2[10001:20000,1] <- PM2.size[,2]
PM2.size2[10001:20000,2] <- colnames(PM2.size)[2]
PM2.size2 <- as.data.frame(PM2.size2)
PM2.size2$Niche_Size <- as.numeric(PM2.size2$Niche_Size)

# Bhattacharyya coefficient to see how different the niche sizes are
# Create an empty matrix

Olap.PM2 <- matrix(NA,2,2)
colnames(Olap.PM2) <- c('SubCluster 1',
                        'SubCluster 2')

rownames(Olap.PM2) <- c('SubCluster 1',
                        'SubCluster 2')

for (sc in 1:2){
  for (sc2 in 1:2){
    Olap.PM2[sc,sc2] <-  bhatt.coeff(PM2.size[,sc], PM2.size[,sc2])
  }
  
}

Olap.PM2

median(PM2.size[,1])
range(PM2.size[,1])

median(PM2.size[,2])
range(PM2.size[,2])


plt.niche <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = PM2.size2,
  x = SubCluster,
  y = Niche_Size,
  pairwise.display = "none",
  #type = "rb",
  #box.args = list(width = 0),
  #point.args = list(alpha = 0),
  xlab = "PMC2 SubClusters",
  ylab = "Niche Size"
  )
ggsave(filename = "../figures/NicheStrategies_PMC2.pdf",
       plot = plt.niche,
       device = cairo_pdf)

print(plt.niche)

# Summary table
sum.PM2 <- summary_table(f.PCAdata.PM.2, our_summary1)
sum.PM2
```
